part.name: Clevis-mount bracket with underside pocket
part.description: Single-piece mechanical bracket comprising a base with four mounting bosses/through-holes, a raised two-lug clevis with coaxial pin holes, gusset/web transitions between base and clevis, and an underside lightening pocket with ribbing. Geometry includes broad planar facets, cylindrical bosses/holes, and numerous blend fillets/chamfers.
part.symmetry_note: Overall near-bilateral symmetry about a longitudinal mid-plane through the clevis gap and between the left/right mounting pairs; small blend details may break exact symmetry.

Section.name: Base & mounting boss system
Section.function intent: Provide the primary interface to a supporting structure via four fasteners; establish stiffness and distribute loads into the rest of the bracket.
Section.physical behavior: Bolt preload is reacted through boss top seats; shear and bending loads are carried through the base shell with blends reducing stress concentration at boss roots and perimeter transitions.
Section.geometry: Elongated base with four corner-ish cylindrical bosses (outer Ø via r=0.8 cylinders) each containing a coaxial through-hole (r=0.4 cylinders). Base has large bottom mounting face and multiple outer sloped/planar side facets with edge rounds (torus blends) along perimeter.
Section.location: Lowest/main body spanning the full footprint; bosses located near the four extremities in plan view.

Section.name: Clevis lug pair (pin interface)
features included: lug outer side faces and inner gap faces
Section.function intent: Provide a clevis interface for a pinned joint; locate and constrain a mating link via a pin passing through the two lugs.
Section.physical behavior: Transfers shear/bearing loads from the pin into the lugs; lug spacing and parallelism constrain mating-part degrees of freedom; rounded profiles reduce notch sensitivity at the lug crown.
Section.geometry: Two parallel lugs separated by a slot/gap, each having a cylindrical through-hole (r=0.75) along the X direction. Lug sides are defined by parallel planes; top/outer edges are largely rounded (cylindrical/filleted).
Section.location: Raised feature near the upper region of the part (seen prominently in isometric), above the base and connected via gussets.

Section.name: Gusset webs & outer transition shell
features included: web/gusset transitions between base and clevis
local chamfers and large exterior blends
Section.function intent: Transfer load between the clevis lugs and the base while controlling stiffness and stress distribution.
Section.physical behavior: Acts primarily in bending and shear; gusset planes provide a short load path and reduce peak stress by spreading forces into the base over a larger area; outer facets also provide clearance envelope and manufacturable draft.
Section.geometry: Multiple large planar facets (top slopes and side facets) blended to adjacent shells; includes a central web plane between lugs and sloped exterior planes on both left/right sides.
Section.location: Mid/upper body between the clevis lugs and the base perimeter, wrapping around the central mass.

Section.name: Underside pocket & ribbing
features included: large underside lightening pocket (open to bottom)
local fillets and small edge rounds inside pocket
Section.function intent: Reduce mass and provide clearance while maintaining stiffness through ribbing; create internal space for neighboring components or tooling access.
Section.physical behavior: Pocket removes low-stress material; ribs carry bending/shear across the cavity by providing local section modulus; internal fillets reduce stress risers at rib-wall junctions.
Section.geometry: Rectangular/rounded-corner underside recess with planar ceiling, multiple sloped/planar walls, and internal planar rib faces; many small blend faces (spheres/tori/cylinders/bsplines) at rib intersections and pocket edges.
Section.location: Underside (bottom view) centrally located pocket spanning much of the part length between the mounting bosses and beneath the gusseted body.
